     │   structured heterogeneous multi-part concept at all; its only parts =  │
     │   re.split(...) usage                                                   │
     │   (line 163) is a free-text recall grader splitting a semicolon-joined  │
     │   string gold answer for a                                              │
     │   "contains all substrings" text match — unrelated to a scalar+set      │
     │   SQL-result multi-part answer.                                         │
     │   Stated plainly: there is no v2 shortcut for D.9. It is a v3-native    │
     │   design problem, addressed                                             │
     │   fresh below, not ported.                                              │
     │ - Regrade design (D.13) — confirmed, not contradicted. v2's regrade.py  │
     │   docstring states                                                      │
     │   explicitly: "Nothing here re-runs the model... No model was re-run:   │
     │   this re-scores" retained                                              │
     │   evidence using current grading logic. That is exactly the shape of    │
     │   the v3 fix proposed below                                             │
     │   (re-apply current grading logic to retained evidence, don't re-run    │
     │   inference) — v2 precedent                                             │
     │   validates the design rather than suggesting a different one.          │
     │                                                                         │

     │ D. Contract changes                                                     │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.1 Registry identity/provenance — two independent layers, not one.     │
     │ 1. Recomputation (mechanical, automatic): load_registry() recomputes    │
     │    the entire registry from                                             │
     │    the three frozen input files via the unmodified selection pipeline   │
     │    and compares it field-for-field                                      │
     │    to the committed JSON, including frozen_date now that it's confirmed │
     │    to be a hardcoded constant                                           │
     │    with nothing legitimate to exclude.                                  │
     │ 2. External approval anchor (human-gated, not automatic): a new,        │
     │    separate record — e.g.                                               │
     │    datasets_v3/PHASE9_APPROVAL.json — holding                           │
     │    {approved_registry_sha256, approved_commit, approved_date}, written  │
     │    by a distinct code path that the normal freeze/regeneration script   │
     │    never                                                                │
     │    calls. This correction builds the mechanism and the check; it does   │
     │    not populate the anchor,                                             │
     │    because Phase 9 isn't approved yet — there's nothing legitimate to   │
     │    anchor to. Once you approve                                          │
     │    Phase 9, populating this file becomes the literal first, separate,   │
     │    auditable action taken (a few                                        │
     │    lines, one commit), distinct from all the code fixes here. Until     │
     │    populated, load_registry()                                           │
     │    reports "approval_pending": true explicitly rather than silently     │
     │    claiming full protection.                                            │
     │ 3. Together these two layers catch what recomputation alone can't: (2)  │
     │    catches "code and registry                                           │
     │    changed together consistently," which (1) cannot.                    │
     │ 4. Bypass closure:                                                      │
     │    scan_strings/scan_operations/scan_compositions/held_out_values stop  │
     │    accepting a bare dict via reg=. They accept only a VerifiedRegistry  │
     │    instance (a thin frozen                                              │
     │    wrapper load_registry() returns after both checks above pass). Fault │
     │    tests get a distinct,                                                │
     │    separately-named test-only constructor                               │
     │    (_unverified_registry_for_tests()) that production code              │
     │    never imports — stated plainly that Python can't hard-enforce this,  │
     │    only naming convention plus a                                        │
     │    fault test asserting no production import path reaches the raw       │
     │    loader.                                                              │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.2 Allowed operations per field — 4 layers, not 2, sourced from a full │
     │ trace of README.                                                        │
     │ 1. field_semantic_operations — what's meaningful for a field, including │
     │    held-out operations                                                  │
     │    where they make sense (e.g. employment → {filter, ranking};          │
     │    child-table fields                                                   │
     │    certifications/processes/services → {filter, aggregation, group_by}; │
     │    categorical company                                                  │
     │    fields → {filter, aggregation, group_by}).                           │
     │ 2. query_level_constructs — argmax_topk, group_by, limit_only tagged as │
     │    structural/                                                          │
     │    query-shape operations that pair with an eligible field from layer 1 │
     │    (limit_only is                                                       │
     │    field-agnostic — arbitrary row sampling, doesn't require a field     │
     │    pairing at all).                                                     │
     │ 3. field_specific_restrictions — sourced verbatim from README, not      │
     │    invented: Primary OEMs                                               │
     │    excluded from group_by/ranking (composite-string reason,             │
     │    README:537-538); Address gets no                                     │
     │    aggregation of any kind (README:538); row_id — join always allowed,  │
     │    filter allowed only                                                  │
     │    when the question explicitly names a record (README:541-543);        │
     │    company — filtering                                                  │
     │    unrestricted.                                                        │
     │ 4. field_training_eligible_operations (derived) = layer 1 minus the 3   │
     │    globally held-out families,                                          │
     │    further constrained by layer 3's named restrictions. This is what    │
     │    future Phase 10/11/12                                                │
     │    generators must intersect against. Evaluation/probe generation       │
     │    (Phase 22) consumes layers 1+3                                       │
     │    directly, unfiltered by the holdout subtraction, since the           │
     │    operation-heldout probe specifically                                 │
     │    needs those constructs to exist in dev/test.                         │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Taxonomy names (filter, aggregation, join, semantic_filter, plus the 3  │
     │ frozen held-out                                                         │
     │ names): traced against every operation-shaped mention in README Phases  │
     │ 12, 14, 18-26, 41 —                                                     │
     │ aggregation and join are the document's own words for real mechanisms   │
     │ (README:264,539,541);                                                   │
     │ no_match/abstention was checked and confirmed to be an                  │
     │ evaluation-outcome axis (Phase 25),                                     │
     │ correctly excluded from this taxonomy. Independently cross-checked      │
     │ against v2's actual                                                     │
     │ taxonomy.py (FILTER_LIST, AGGREGATE covering                            │
     │ count/sum/group-by/argmax/top-k,                                        │
     │ SEMANTIC_FILTER for free-text columns) — the two sources converge on    │
     │ the same core names, and v2                                             │
     │ surfaces semantic_filter as the right category for                      │
     │ companies.product_or_service (a free-text                               │
     │ field with no v3 precedent otherwise). Still flagged for your explicit  │
     │ sign-off since neither                                                  │
     │ README nor v2 assembles this exact list as a single named per-field     │
     │ contract — Phase 9 is where it                                          │
     │ gets assembled for the first time, now grounded in two independent,     │
     │ converging sources rather than                                          │
     │ invented from nothing.                                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.3 Training eligibility. As above (layer 4), kept structurally         │
     │ separate from semantic validity                                         │
     │ (layer 1) so Phase 22's probe and future training generators consume    │
     │ the correct layer.                                                      │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.4 SQL operation detection — comment-safe lexer, not raw stripping. A  │
     │ left-to-right scanner                                                   │
     │ that replaces (never deletes) each '...' string literal, "..." / `...`  │
     │ / [...]                                                                 │
     │ quoted-identifier span, -- ... line comment, and /* ... */ block        │
     │ comment with a single space —                                           │
     │ preserving token boundaries so GROUP/**/BY becomes GROUP BY             │
     │ (space-separated), not GROUPBY                                          │
     │ (concatenated). Keyword-boundary regex (\bGROUP\s+BY\b, \bORDER\s+BY\b, │
     │ \bLIMIT\b,                                                              │
     │ case-insensitive) then runs on the cleaned remainder. Full test matrix: │
     │ GROUP/**/BY (detect),                                                   │
     │ GROUP\nBY (detect), GROUP  BY (detect), SELECT 'LIMIT' AS x (must NOT   │
     │ detect — inside string                                                  │
     │ literal), SELECT "GROUP BY" FROM t (must NOT detect — quoted            │
     │ identifier), SELECT `GROUP BY` FROM t                                   │
     │ (must NOT detect — backtick identifier), SELECT [GROUP BY] FROM t (must │
     │ NOT detect — bracket                                                    │
     │ identifier), SELECT group_id FROM t (must NOT detect — word boundary    │
     │ already excludes this),                                                 │
     │ escaped-quote cases ('it''s', "a""b") handled correctly by the          │
     │ scanner's escape-doubling rule.                                         │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.5 Exposure scanner. List-only: scan_strings(list[str]) -> report. A   │
     │ bare str raises                                                         │
     │ TypeError naming the expected type — single, non-contradictory contract │
     │ (Rev 1's self-contradiction                                             │
     │ is fully resolved, not just relabeled).                                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.6 Exposure-report assertions — three typed functions, not one generic │
     │ one. Each report shape                                                  │
     │ already has its own evidence counter in the current code                │
     │ (strings_scanned, sql_scanned,                                          │
     │ sets_scanned/composition_violations — confirmed to exist now, not       │
     │ hypothetical):                                                          │
     │ assert_value_scan_verified(report),                                     │
     │ assert_operation_scan_verified(report),                                 │
     │ assert_composition_scan_verified(report) — each hardcodes which fields  │
     │ must be present/consistent                                              │
     │ for its own shape. No caller ever names an arbitrary counter field,     │
     │ closing the                                                             │
     │ counter="wrong_field" bypass. Four states per type: pending             │
     │ (scanned:false,count:null — valid,                                      │
     │ never a pass), verified-zero (scanned:true, evidence counter >0,        │
     │ exposure_count:0,                                                       │
     │ internally consistent per-item/total), exposure-detected (fails),       │
     │ malformed (missing/inconsistent                                         │
     │ fields — fails).                                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.7 Exposure normalization. Unicode-normalize (NFC) → casefold →        │
     │ collapse internal whitespace                                            │
     │ runs → substring match, applied to every held-out literal against every │
     │ model-visible rendered                                                  │
     │ string (not only raw KB cells — rendering/copying can alter             │
     │ representation even from ASCII                                          │
     │ sources). "AS9100", "as9100", " AS9100 " all match; unrelated           │
     │ substrings do not. Flagged for                                          │
     │ approval since this is a real scientific definition of "exposure," not  │
     │ a mechanically-derived                                                  │
     │ default — biased toward over-detection deliberately (a false positive   │
     │ costs one extra row to                                                  │
     │ inspect; a false negative is an actual leak).                           │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.8 Logical fingerprint (lfp2). Canonicalized logical_components folded │
     │ into the hash.                                                          │
     │ Commutative operands (two ANDed or two ORed predicates) sort before     │
     │ hashing so reordering doesn't                                           │
     │ change the fingerprint; the operator itself and any differing           │
     │ predicate/value do change it. Nested                                    │
     │ trees (A AND (B OR C) vs (A AND B) OR C) hash by canonical tree form,   │
     │ not flattened. Missing/                                                 │
     │ incomplete logical_components fails closed rather than silently falling │
     │ back to a weaker hash.                                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.9 Multipart representation — concrete, not deferred, and confirmed to │
     │ have no v2 precedent                                                    │
     │ (v2's grade.py never solved a heterogeneous structured multi-part case  │
     │ — see Context). gold_sql for a multipart task remains                   │
     │ one query (preserving Phase 12's "D's target is a query" framing)       │
     │ structured as                                                           │
     │ UNION ALL across parts, each branch prefixed with a literal             │
     │ discriminator column                                                    │
     │ (SELECT 'count' AS part_id, CAST(n AS TEXT) AS val FROM (...) UNION ALL │
     │ SELECT 'companies', company FROM (...)). The executed SQLResult is      │
     │ grouped by part_id post-execution into independent                      │
     │ per-part SQLResult slices (each with its own column set and row count — │
     │ this is what lets a                                                     │
     │ 1-row scalar part and a 3-row set part coexist without forcing a shared │
     │ rectangular shape). Each                                                │
     │ slice is graded against its own parts[] entry's                         │
     │ answer_type/target_columns via the existing                             │
     │ compare_results machinery unchanged (each slice is graded independently │
     │ as a self-contained set/                                                │
     │ scalar/top_k answer, not a new grading algorithm).                      │
     │ EvalRecord.execution_result retains the full                            │
     │ tagged (pre-split) row set as-is — no new field needed for the data     │
     │ itself, only the parts                                                  │
     │ metadata field needed to know how to re-split it later. This design is  │
     │ explicitly scoped to Phase                                              │
     │ 9's job — freezing the metadata contract and the post-execution         │
     │ representation grade_v3.py                                              │
     │ consumes. How C's raw model completion gets parsed into this same       │
     │ tagged-row representation is a                                          │
     │ Phase 11/13 renderer/parser question, out of Phase 9's scope — stated   │
     │ explicitly rather than                                                  │
     │ silently assumed solved.                                                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.10 Extra-part rule — settled now, not deferred. Extends the existing, │
     │ already-frozen                                                          │
     │ precedent (phase7_grader_tests.py's                                     │
     │ metrics_differ_semantic_right_schema_wrong: an extra column             │
     │ scores task_result_correctness=1.0 but                                  │
     │ strict_result_schema_accuracy=0.0): an extra,                           │
     │ undeclared part present in the executed/tagged result beyond what       │
     │ parts[] declares does not                                               │
     │ fail task_result_correctness (each declared part is still graded        │
     │ independently and correctly) but                                        │
     │ does fail strict_result_schema_accuracy (output includes something      │
     │ outside the declared schema).                                           │
     │ Missing required parts[] metadata on a multi_part-typed item fails      │
     │ closed with a clear error —                                             │
     │ never silently falls back to legacy per-column grading. Legacy fallback │
     │ (flattened                                                              │
     │ target_columns-as-parts) applies only to items explicitly predating     │
     │ parts_list_v1 (a fixed,                                                 │
     │ named allowlist of legacy fixture IDs, not "any item missing parts"),   │
     │ so a future generator bug                                               │
     │ that omits parts[] cannot silently masquerade as a legacy item.         │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.11 Grading. As D.9/D.10. GRADER_VERSION bumped grade_v3.0 →           │
     │ grade_v3.1.                                                             │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.12 EvalRecord/result schema. Optional parts: tuple | None = None,     │
     │ backward-compatible                                                     │
     │ from_dict default. build_fixtures() extended with a                     │
     │ populated-execution_result multipart                                    │
     │ fixture pair specifically to prove regrade() recomputation: one         │
     │ deliberately-wrong multipart                                            │
     │ answer that the current (buggy) grader would have scored correct,       │

※ recap: We're fixing Phase 9's holdout registry so it passes independent audit before approving it; I've drafted a Revision 4 correction plan grounded in README and v2 precedent. Next: you review and approve the plan file so I can implement it. (disable recaps in /config)

❯                                                                               
                                                                                
                                                                                
  Revision 3 is much closer, but I would not approve it unchanged. It resolves  
  several earlier findings at the plan level. Three technical contracts still   
  need correction; I reproduced the key problems using synthetic, in-memory     
  examples.                                                                     
  1. The operation subtraction still leaves a loophole                          
  D.2 proposes:                                                                 
  employment semantic operations = {filter, ranking}                            
  held-out families = {argmax_topk, group_by, limit_only}                       
  Subtracting those sets leaves ranking training-eligible, because ranking and  
  argmax_topk are different names.                                              
  The distinction between semantic validity and training eligibility is now     
  correct. The missing piece is an explicit mapping between semantic operations 
  and their required query constructs.                                          
  Required amendment:                                                           
  - Resolve a top-k ranking to argmax_topk before checking training             
  eligibility.                                                                  
  - Distinguish allowed aggregation from aggregation requiring held-out         
  constructs.                                                                   
  - Apply the query-level exclusion independently—especially for field-agnostic 
  LIMIT.                                                                        
  - Test actual tasks and SQL, not just whether forbidden names appear in the   
  policy lists.                                                                 
  2. Tagged multipart results are workable, but the representation is not       
  complete                                                                      
  I tested the proposed UNION ALL approach. It successfully separates parts     
  with different row counts, but it does not automatically give them            
  independent column schemas.                                                   
  For example, the proposed count-plus-companies query returns:                 
  columns: part_id, val                                                         
  rows:    count,     "3"                                                       
           companies, Alpha                                                     
           companies, Beta                                                      
  The second branch’s company column name is not retained. A branch returning   
  both company and county also fails unless every branch has the same number of 
  result columns.                                                               
  Before implementation, specify:                                               
  - The common tagged-column layout and explicit mapping to each part’s target  
  columns.                                                                      
  - Numeric handling. The proposed CAST(... AS TEXT) changes 3 into "3"; the    
  current scalar grader treats those as different.                              
  - How empty parts are represented or interpreted. An empty branch and an

  - How top-k ordering survives execution, grouping and serialization.

  retained for strict-schema regrading.

  Claude says:                                                                  
  C parsing is a Phase 11/13 concern and outside Phase 9.                       
  That is partially fair.                                                       
  Phase 9 does not need to implement C parsing now.                             
  But Phase 9 does need to freeze a modality-independent multipart semantic     
  contract.                                                                     
  Otherwise D gets:                                                             
  ```sql                                                                        
  UNION ALL + part_id                                                           
  ```                                                                           
  while C later invents a different concept of a “part,” and                    
  regrading/reporting has to reconcile them.                                    
  The cleaner layering is:                                                      
  ```sql                                                                        
  Phase 9:                                                                      
      logical multipart result contract                                         
                                                                                
  D:                                                                            
      SQL encoding -> logical multipart result                                  
                                                                                
  C:                                                                            
      direct-answer parsing -> same logical multipart result                    
  ```                                                                           
  So Phase 9 need not implement C's parser, but it should define the            
  intermediate representation both C and D eventually produce.                  
  That will make EvalRecord, grading, and regrading modality-independent.

    new grading logic.

    (load_candidate_registry_for_phase9_audit() vs. load_registry()), the latter
    raising Phase9NotApproved when the anchor is absent rather than returning a
    usable object with a pending flag. Added deep-immutability via
    canonical-JSON-text storage.

    Unicode (ＡＳ９１００) while NFKC correctly folds it.

  D. Contract changes

  D.1 Registry identity/provenance — two APIs with genuinely different 
  guarantees, not one loader
  with a boolean flag. Rev 4's load_registry() returning a usable
  VerifiedRegistry plus a
  "approval_pending": true flag conflated "content-verified" with "approved" — a
  candidate that
  merely passed recomputation could still be consumed by production code,
  defeating the point of an
  approval gate. Split into two named functions with different contracts:
  1. load_candidate_registry_for_phase9_audit() — usable now, before approval.
     Runs
     recomputation (recomputes the entire registry from the three frozen input
     files via the
     unmodified selection pipeline and compares it field-for-field to the
     committed JSON, including
     frozen_date now that it's confirmed to be a hardcoded constant with nothing
     legitimate to
     exclude) plus schema/internal-consistency checks. No approval anchor
     required or checked. This is
     what --check, fault tests, and synthetic validation use.
  2. load_registry() — the production/Phase-10+ entry point. Requires a
     separate, external approval
     record (below) to exist and match; raises Phase9NotApproved if the anchor 
     is absent —
     it does not return a partially-usable object with a pending flag. If the
     anchor exists but
     doesn't match the current registry's recomputed hash, it raises a distinct
     tamper error. This
     makes "Phase 10 cannot start before Phase 9 approval" a mechanical property
     of the loader Phase
     10+ code would naturally reach for, not a documentation convention someone
     could bypass by
     calling the wrong function.
  3. External approval anchor: a new, separate record —
     datasets_v3/PHASE9_APPROVAL.json — holding
     {approved_registry_sha256, approved_commit, approved_date}, written by a
     distinct code path the
     normal freeze/regeneration script never calls. approved_commit is the SHA
     of the correction
     commit that introduces the exact registry content being approved — not a
     later status-
     advancement commit — so the lineage reads candidate commit → approval
     record → (separately) the
     commit that advances LAST_COMPLETED_PHASE in CLAUDE.md. This correction 
     builds the mechanism
     and both functions; it does not populate the anchor, because Phase 9 isn't
     approved yet.
     Populating it becomes the literal first, separate, auditable action once
     you approve — a few
     lines, one commit, distinct from all the code fixes here. A file inside the
     same writable repo is
     not an external security boundary by itself, so this is described precisely
     as a separately
     reviewed approval record anchored to the reviewed commit, not a
     cryptographic guarantee.
  4. Bypass closure:
     scan_strings/scan_operations/scan_compositions/held_out_values stop
     accepting a bare dict via reg=. They accept only a
     VerifiedCandidateRegistry instance (the
     thin wrapper function 1 returns). Fault tests get a distinct,
     separately-named test-only
     constructor (_unverified_registry_for_tests()) that production code never
     imports — stated
     plainly that Python can't hard-enforce this, only naming convention plus a
     fault test asserting no
     production import path reaches the raw loader.
  5. Deep immutability, not just a frozen wrapper: @dataclass(frozen=True) only
     blocks reassigning
     the top-level attribute, not mutating a nested dict/list inside it. Fix:
     the wrapper stores the
     canonical registry as serialized JSON text; every accessor (.section(name),
     etc.) returns
     json.loads() of that stored text — a fresh deep copy on every read, so a
     caller mutating a
     returned object can never corrupt the stored original. Regression test:
     call an accessor, mutate
     the returned object in place, call the accessor again, assert the second
     result is unaffected.

  D.2 Allowed operations per field — 4 layers, and the subtraction now provably 
  works, because
  there's only one vocabulary, not two. Rev 3/4's flaw: the semantic layer said
  employment → {filter, ranking} while the held-out-families constant is
  {argmax_topk, group_by, limit_only} —
  "ranking" != "argmax_topk", so a literal set-subtraction semantic - held_out
  would never actually
  remove ranking, silently leaving it training-eligible (the opposite of
  intended, and worse than
  before). Fix: stop inventing softer synonyms for the semantic layer — reuse 
  the exact frozen
  construct names everywhere, so eligibility subtraction is a plain,
  provably-correct set difference
  on identical strings, not a translation the code could get wrong:
  1. field_semantic_operations — what's meaningful for a field, including
     held-out operations
     where they make sense, named with the same literal strings as
     HELD_OUT_OPERATIONS
     (holdout_v3.py's existing frozen constant) wherever applicable: employment
     →
     {filter, argmax_topk} (not "ranking"); child-table fields
     (certifications/processes/
     services) and categorical company fields → {filter, aggregation, group_by}.
     aggregation here means ungrouped scalar aggregation only (COUNT/SUM with no
     GROUP BY)
     — a sibling of group_by, never a parent/hierarchy containing it, resolving
     the ambiguity
     directly: the three already-frozen held-out names (argmax_topk, group_by,
     limit_only) are
     never subtypes of anything else in this taxonomy, they're leaves.
  2. query_level_constructs — argmax_topk, group_by, limit_only, tagged as
     structural/
     query-shape operations that pair with an eligible field from layer 1
     (limit_only is
     field-agnostic — arbitrary row sampling, doesn't require a field pairing at
     all, so it's excluded
     globally regardless of any per-field policy — see the fault test in E for
     this specific case).
  3. field_specific_restrictions — sourced verbatim from README, not invented:
     Primary OEMs
     excluded from group_by/argmax_topk (composite-string reason,
     README:537-538); Address gets
     no aggregation of any kind (README:538); row_id — join always allowed,
     filter allowed
     only when the question explicitly names a record (README:541-543); company
     — filtering
     unrestricted.
  4. field_training_eligible_operations (derived) = field_semantic_operations[f]
     - HELD_OUT_OPERATIONS (literal set difference on the shared vocabulary,
     machine-tested by asserting
     this equation for every field), further constrained by layer 3's named
     restrictions. Evaluation/
     probe generation (Phase 22) consumes layers 1+3 directly, unfiltered by the
     subtraction, since the
     operation-heldout probe specifically needs those constructs to exist in
     dev/test.
  5. This per-field map is a candidate-generation-time heuristic, never the 
     authoritative
     eligibility gate. The real, existing gate — already frozen, fixed in D.4 —
     is running the actual
     SQL-construct scanner (operation_families_present) against a task's actual 
     rendered gold_sql
     at generation time; D.2's map only narrows which field+operation
     combinations are worth
     attempting to generate in the first place. Fault tests must exercise real
     constructed SQL strings
     through the scanner (e.g. a bare SELECT company FROM companies LIMIT 5 —
     field-agnostic,
     excluded regardless of which field's policy was consulted), not merely
     check whether a forbidden
     name string appears in a policy list.

  Taxonomy names (filter, aggregation, join, semantic_filter, plus the 3 frozen
  held-out
  names): traced against every operation-shaped mention in README Phases 12, 14,
  18-26, 41 —
  aggregation and join are the document's own words for real mechanisms
  (README:264,539,541);
  no_match/abstention was checked and confirmed to be an evaluation-outcome axis
  (Phase 25),
  correctly excluded from this taxonomy. Independently cross-checked against
  v2's actual
  taxonomy.py (FILTER_LIST, AGGREGATE covering count/sum/group-by/argmax/top-k,
  SEMANTIC_FILTER for free-text columns) — the two sources converge on the same
  core names, and v2
  surfaces semantic_filter as the right category for
  companies.product_or_service (a free-text
  field with no v3 precedent otherwise). Still flagged for your explicit 
  sign-off since neither
  README nor v2 assembles this exact list as a single named per-field contract —
  Phase 9 is where it
  gets assembled for the first time, now grounded in two independent, converging
  sources rather than
  invented from nothing.

  D.3 Training eligibility. As above (layer 4), kept structurally separate from
  semantic validity
  (layer 1) so Phase 22's probe and future training generators consume the
  correct layer.

  D.4 SQL operation detection — comment-safe lexer, not raw stripping. A
  left-to-right scanner
  that replaces (never deletes) each '...' string literal, "..." / `...` / [...]
  quoted-identifier span, -- ... line comment, and /* ... */ block comment with
  a single space —
  preserving token boundaries so GROUP/**/BY becomes GROUP BY (space-separated),
  not GROUPBY
  (concatenated). Keyword-boundary regex (\bGROUP\s+BY\b, \bORDER\s+BY\b,
  \bLIMIT\b,
  case-insensitive) then runs on the cleaned remainder. Full test matrix:
  GROUP/**/BY (detect),
  GROUP\nBY (detect), GROUP  BY (detect), SELECT 'LIMIT' AS x (must NOT detect —
  inside string
  literal), SELECT "GROUP BY" FROM t (must NOT detect — quoted identifier),
  SELECT `GROUP BY` FROM t
  (must NOT detect — backtick identifier), SELECT [GROUP BY] FROM t (must NOT
  detect — bracket
  identifier), SELECT group_id FROM t (must NOT detect — word boundary already
  excludes this),
  escaped-quote cases ('it''s', "a""b") handled correctly by the scanner's
  escape-doubling rule.

  D.5 Exposure scanner. List-only: scan_strings(list[str]) -> report. A bare str
  raises
  TypeError naming the expected type — single, non-contradictory contract (Rev
  1's self-contradiction
  is fully resolved, not just relabeled).

  D.6 Exposure-report assertions — three typed functions, not one generic one.
  Each report shape
  already has its own evidence counter in the current code (strings_scanned,
  sql_scanned,
  sets_scanned/composition_violations — confirmed to exist now, not
  hypothetical):
  assert_value_scan_verified(report), assert_operation_scan_verified(report),
  assert_composition_scan_verified(report) — each hardcodes which fields must be
  present/consistent
  for its own shape. No caller ever names an arbitrary counter field, closing
  the
  counter="wrong_field" bypass. Four states per type: pending
  (scanned:false,count:null — valid,
  never a pass), verified-zero (scanned:true, evidence counter >0,
  exposure_count:0,
  internally consistent per-item/total), exposure-detected (fails), malformed
  (missing/inconsistent
  fields — fails).

  D.7 Exposure normalization — NFKC, not NFC (verified, not assumed). Ran the
  actual case:
  unicodedata.normalize('NFC', 'ＡＳ９１００') returns the fullwidth string
  unchanged (does not
  equal 'AS9100'); NFKC on the same input correctly folds it to 'AS9100'. NFC
  only normalizes
  canonical equivalence (e.g. accented composition); it does not fold
  compatibility variants
  (fullwidth forms, and similar). Corrected pipeline:
  Unicode-compatibility-normalize (NFKC) →
  casefold → collapse internal whitespace runs → substring match, applied to
  every held-out literal
  against every model-visible rendered string (not only raw KB cells —
  rendering/copying can alter
  representation even from ASCII sources), confined to the scanning step only
  (never mutates the
  actual training text). "AS9100", "as9100", " AS9100 ", "ＡＳ９１００" all
  match; unrelated
  substrings do not. Flagged for approval since this is a real scientific
  definition of
  "exposure," not a mechanically-derived default — biased toward over-detection
  deliberately (a false
  positive costs one extra row to inspect; a false negative is an actual leak).

  D.8 Logical fingerprint (lfp2). Canonicalized logical_components folded into
  the hash.
  Commutative operands (two ANDed or two ORed predicates) sort before hashing so
  reordering doesn't
  change the fingerprint; the operator itself and any differing predicate/value
  do change it. Nested
  trees (A AND (B OR C) vs (A AND B) OR C) hash by canonical tree form, not
  flattened. Missing/
  incomplete logical_components fails closed rather than silently falling back
  to a weaker hash.

  D.9 Multipart representation — redesigned in this revision. The 
  UNION-ALL-with-discriminator
  design from Rev 3/4 is withdrawn; it doesn't work. Constructive proof: UNION 
  ALL requires equal
  column arity across every branch, so a scalar part (val) and a two-column part
  (company, county)
  cannot share one result shape without padding; the shared part_id, val schema
  also throws away
  each part's real column names, forces every value through CAST(... AS TEXT)
  (turning 3 into
  "3", which the existing scalar grader's _SCALAR_OK type check would then treat
  as a different
  value than an untouched gold 3), and — worse — would require the model's own 
  predicted SQL to
  independently reproduce that exact discriminator/CAST convention just to be
  gradable, teaching an
  artificial SQL-shape requirement that has nothing to do with the actual
  question. Withdrawn.

  Replacement design: an ordered/keyed collection of independently-executed, 
  independently-typed
  per-part results — no shared schema, no discriminator, no casting.
  - gold_sql for a multi_part task is a dict keyed by part_id, one independently
    normal SQL
    string per declared part (e.g. {"count": "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ...", 
    "companies": "SELECT company FROM ..."}), each executed on its own,
    producing its own natural SQLResult
    with its own real column names and native types. This still honors Phase
    12's "D's target is a
    query" framing as its natural generalization for the multi-part case: a
    keyed sequence of
    queries, not one query straining to represent several shapes at once.
  - The model's predicted SQL for a multi-part task is a sequence of statements
    (split on
    top-level ; using the same comment/quote-aware lexer built for D.4, so a
    semicolon inside a
    string literal is never mistaken for a statement boundary), executed in the
    order the question
    presents the parts (order is part of the frozen task, known to both the
    model via the prompt and
    the grader via parts[] — nothing is invented at grading time). Each
    statement is paired
    positionally with the corresponding declared part.
  - Grading: a new thin wrapper, grade_multipart(item, pred_results: dict, 
    gold_results: dict) -> GradeResult, calls the existing, unmodified
    compare_results once per declared part (its own
    answer_type/target_columns), and requires every declared part correct — no
    new comparison
    algorithm, full reuse of frozen Phase 7 semantics per part.
  - Empty vs. omitted parts are now cleanly distinguishable, closing the Rev 4
    ambiguity: an emitted
    statement that executes and returns 0 rows is a legitimate empty-set answer
    for that part, graded
    normally; an omitted statement (fewer statements than declared parts) is a
    missing-required-part
    failure. No shared-table ambiguity to resolve.
  - Top-k ordering, real column names, and native types are preserved
    automatically — each part's
    SQLResult is exactly what that part's own SELECT naturally returns, nothing
    is regrouped or
    reinterpreted after the fact.
  - EvalRecord.execution_result for a multi-part item becomes a dict keyed by
    part_id, each value
    the natural (columns, rows) pair for that part — still one JSON-serializable
    field, still
    trivially round-trips through save/reload/regrade; the parts metadata field
    says which
    answer_type/target_columns apply to which key.
  - Modality-independent contract, addressing the layering concern directly:
    Phase 9 freezes the
    property that a multi-part answer is a part_id-keyed collection of 
    independently-typed
    part-results, each graded via the existing single-part compare_results 
    semantics using that
    part's own answer_type/target_columns. D produces this via a keyed sequence
    of independent
    SQL executions (above). How C's raw model completion gets parsed into this 
    same keyed-result
    shape remains a Phase 11/13 concern, correctly out of Phase 9's scope — but
    Phase 9 now freezes
    the target representation both modalities must produce, not just D's
    mechanism, so grading,
    EvalRecord, and regrading are written once and work for either modality
    without later
    reconciliation. (Confirmed: no v2 precedent exists for this either way — see
    Context.)

  D.10 Extra-part rule — settled now, not deferred. Extends the existing,
  already-frozen
  precedent (phase7_grader_tests.py's
  metrics_differ_semantic_right_schema_wrong: an extra column
  scores task_result_correctness=1.0 but strict_result_schema_accuracy=0.0): an
  extra,
  undeclared part present in the executed/tagged result beyond what parts[]
  declares does not
  fail task_result_correctness (each declared part is still graded independently
  and correctly) but
  does fail strict_result_schema_accuracy (output includes something outside the
  declared schema).
  Missing required parts[] metadata on a multi_part-typed item fails closed with
  a clear error —
  never silently falls back to legacy per-column grading. Legacy fallback
  (flattened
  target_columns-as-parts) applies only to items explicitly predating
  parts_list_v1 (a fixed,
  named allowlist of legacy fixture IDs, not "any item missing parts"), so a
  future generator bug
  that omits parts[] cannot silently masquerade as a legacy item.

  D.11 Grading. As D.9/D.10. GRADER_VERSION bumped grade_v3.0 → grade_v3.1.

  D.12 EvalRecord/result schema. Optional parts: tuple | None = None,
  backward-compatible
  from_dict default. build_fixtures() extended with a populated-execution_result
  multipart
  fixture pair specifically to prove regrade() recomputation: one
  deliberately-wrong multipart
  answer that the current (buggy) grader would have scored correct, regraded
  under the fixed
  grader to confirm it now scores incorrect — proving the regrade path genuinely
  recomputes rather
  than re-stamping provenance on a stale score.

  D.13 Verification/regrading. regrade() re-invokes
  compare_results/grade_structured
  against retained execution_result/gold (per-part where applicable) instead of
  keeping the
  recorded outcome for well-formed predictions. Raw prediction and gold remain
  untouched (existing
  _replace() invariant preserved).

  E. Validation and regression matrix

  Contract changed: Registry verification (two-function split + approval anchor
  +
  bypass closure + deep immutability)
  Dependency: Phase 9 fault tests
  Tests to rerun: load_candidate_registry_for_phase9_audit(): current
  registry→pass; stale v3.0→fail; mutated v3.1 (one value flipped, upstream
  hashes untouched)→fail; malformed/missing-section→fail; duplicate selected
  value→fail. load_registry(): no approval anchor→raises Phase9NotApproved;
  anchor present but mismatched→raises tamper error. Direct reg= dict (not the
  wrapper type)→raises. Mutate an accessor's returned object, re-read, confirm
  original unaffected (deep immutability)
  Artifact/hash impact: HOLDOUT_REGISTRY_v3.json hash changes
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Contract changed: Allowed-operations 4-layer contract
  Dependency: Phase 9 fault tests
  Tests to rerun: missing-field-policy→fail; unsupported operation→fail;
  field_training_eligible[f] == field_semantic[f] -  HELD_OUT_OPERATIONS holds
  for every field (exact set-equality, not "name doesn't appear"); limit_only
  excluded globally via the real SQL scanner on an actual field-agnostic LIMIT
  query, not via a per-field policy lookup; Primary OEMs/Address/row_id
  restrictions enforced

  ### The remaining blockers                                                    
                                                                                
  **1. Required-part execution failure semantics are not frozen.**              
                                                                                
  Claude explicitly marks this as a gap. We still need exact behavior when one  
  multipart SQL statement:                                                      
                                                                                
  -  fails to parse,                                                            
  -  contains multiple statements,                                              
  -  returns SQL error,                                                         
  -  times out,                                                                 
  -  is omitted,                                                                
  -  produces malformed result.                                                 
                                                                                
  The scientifically clean default is likely:                                   
                                                                                
  > If any required part fails, the entire multipart task is incorrect and      
  remains in the denominator, while the failing part and failure reason are     
  retained.                                                                     
                                                                                
  But Codex should verify that against the existing Phase 7/8 failure taxonomy  
  rather than us inventing another code.                                        
                                                                                
  ---                                                                           
                                                                                
  **2. Operation holdout scanning is not explicitly applied across every SQL    
  part.**                                                                       
                                                                                
  This is essential.                                                            
                                                                                
  For:                                                                          
                                                                                
  ```                                                                           
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  ```                                                                           
  part_1 -> ordinary filter                                                     
  part_2 -> GROUP BY                                                            
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  the **whole training task must be excluded**.                                 
                                                                                
  Likewise:                                                                     
                                                                                
  ```                                                                           
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  ```                                                                           
  part_1 -> clean                                                               
  part_2 -> ORDER BY ... LIMIT                                                  
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
  must not sneak into D training.                                               
                                                                                
  The authoritative decision needs to be based on the u                         
  ──── (211 lines hidden) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── 
  ly the frozen superset exclusion to that set. Dividing a task into parts must 
  not bypass the held-out combination.                                          
                                                                                
  Retain per-part structure and join-arity information; combining component     
  sets must not invent a join that never occurred. [Frozen superset rule (line  
  729)]\(/home/sm11926/GNEM\_Finetuning/README.md:729)                          
                                                                                
  ### 4. Define insufficient-evidence behavior for all regrading                
                                                                                
  The new fixture pair proves one path. It does not establish what happens to   
  other records lacking retained results.                                       
                                                                                
  Add this rule:                                                                
                                                                                
  > Regrading requires sufficient evidence for the applicable outcome. For      
  normal answer comparison, retain actual prediction/gold columns, rows, types, 
  ordering and part identities. If required evidence is missing, report an      
  explicit regrading failure and do not emit a newly certified score.           
                                                                                
  Crucially, missing audit evidence is **not automatically an incorrect model   
  answer**. Do not silently replace it with zero, drop it from the denominator, 
  or retain the old score with a new grader stamp.                              
                                                                                
  Known generation failures can still be reclassified from sufficient           
  raw-output and stop evidence without requiring SQL results.                   
                                                                                
  Require serialization/reload/regrade tests for both complete and insufficient 
  evidence.                                                                     
                                                                                
  ### Implementation details—not another design review                          
                                                                                
  The remaining registry-loader separation, immutable storage, NFKC scanning,   
  operation vocabulary, versioning and independent recomputation proposals are  
  suitable for implementation.

  Codex's scanner integration bug — reproduced live, exactly as described. I ran
  the actual scan_operations against a synthetic {"count": "...", "companies": 
  "SELECT company FROM companies LIMIT 5"} dict:
  passing the dict directly:   0 exposures  (silently scanned the KEYS
  "count"/"companies")
  passing dict.values():       1 exposure   (correctly caught the bare LIMIT)
  This is a real, exploitable hole my own D.9 redesign introduces — a dict is
  iterable, scan_operations does for i, s in enumerate(strings), and iterating a
  dict gives you its keys. Accepted, and it's serious: this would silently let
  a held-out construct into training the moment gold_sql became a part_id-keyed
  dict instead of a list.

  Codex's composition claim is logically sound (I didn't need to "run" it — it
  follows directly from the frozen superset rule I re-read at README.md's Phase
  23 section: "For each held-out set H and every training set T: assert not H ⊆ 
  T" — a multi-part task is one logical training item, so T must be the union of
  every part's components, not each part checked in isolation). Checking parts
  separately would let {certifications} in part A and {processes} in part B slip
  past the {certifications, processes} holdout entirely.

  Codex's execution-failure point is grounded correctly — I re-read
  grade_v3.py's actual grade_structured (lines ~100-175): it re-raises
  X.ScopeError rather than swallowing it, and uses the existing closed status
  vocabulary (SQL_error, parse_failure, generation_failure, truncated_output,
  invalid_output) for everything else. Multi-part failure handling should reuse
  this exact vocabulary per-part, not invent a new one, and must preserve the
  re-raise-don't-swallow rule for scope violations.

  Where I'm pushing back: Codex's proposed new status
  not_regradable_due_to_missing_evidence for the insufficient-evidence case. I
  checked — CLAUDE.md §25 freezes a closed 8-value status vocabulary for
  evaluation items (correct/incorrect/generation_failure/parse_failure/SQL_error
  /timeout/truncated_output/invalid_output) with a hard assertion scored + 
  failed == expected_probe_size over exactly those. Adding a 9th status would
  break that frozen contract, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that grading-rule
  changes need your approval, not a silent addition. The substance of Codex's
  requirement is right (never silently relabel an unverifiable old score as
  freshly recomputed), but the mechanism needs to avoid the closed enum: I'm
  proposing a separate, non-authoritative regrade_outcome field (recomputed /
  insufficient_evidence / not_attempted) that sits alongside status, leaving the
  original frozen status/scores untouched when evidence is missing, rather than
  a new status value. Flagging this as a resolved protocol-consistency call,
  not inventing around it.

  ChatGPT's new point (gold/prediction asymmetry — keyed dict vs. positional 
  statements) is valid and not redundant with anything already in the plan:
  accepted as its own explicit sub-contract with a dedicated test matrix (wrong
  order, too few/too many statements, semicolon-in-quotes, empty statement,

     │ - validation_v3/EVAL_STACK_VALIDATION_v3.md — updated pinned hashes,    │
     │   old→new lineage table.                                                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ MAY CHANGE                                                              │
     │ - finetune/context_renderer_v3.py — only if it calls scan_strings with  │
     │   a scalar string today                                                 │
     │   (check call sites first).                                             │
     │ - PROVENANCE_v3.md — optional per CLAUDE.md §30, only if you want the   │
     │   correction recorded there.                                            │
     │                                                                         │
     │ VERIFIED UNAFFECTED                                                     │
     │ - select_holdouts() and all combinatorial-optimizer logic in            │
     │   holdout_v3.py (no fix touches it —                                    │
     │   confirmed by design, verified by diff in F).                          │
     │ - finetune/sqlexec_v3.py, finetune/kb_v3.py, Phase 1-6 scripts,         │
     │   datasets_v3/canonical_records_v3.jsonl,                               │
