     │ D. Contract changes                                                     │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.1 Registry identity/provenance — two APIs with genuinely different    │
     │ guarantees, not one loader                                              │
     │ with a boolean flag. Rev 4's load_registry() returning a usable         │
     │ VerifiedRegistry plus a                                                 │
     │ "approval_pending": true flag conflated "content-verified" with         │
     │ "approved" — a candidate that                                           │
     │ merely passed recomputation could still be consumed by production code, │
     │ defeating the point of an                                               │
     │ approval gate. Split into two named functions with different contracts: │
     │ 1. load_candidate_registry_for_phase9_audit() — usable now, before      │
     │    approval. Runs                                                       │
     │    recomputation (recomputes the entire registry from the three frozen  │
     │    input files via the                                                  │
     │    unmodified selection pipeline and compares it field-for-field to the │
     │    committed JSON, including                                            │
     │    frozen_date now that it's confirmed to be a hardcoded constant with  │
     │    nothing legitimate to                                                │
     │    exclude) plus schema/internal-consistency checks. No approval anchor │
     │    required or checked. This is                                         │
     │    what --check, fault tests, and synthetic validation use.             │
     │ 2. load_registry() — the production/Phase-10+ entry point. Requires a   │
     │    separate, external approval                                          │
     │    record (below) to exist and match; raises Phase9NotApproved if the   │
     │    anchor is absent —                                                   │
     │    it does not return a partially-usable object with a pending flag. If │
     │    the anchor exists but                                                │
     │    doesn't match the current registry's recomputed hash, it raises a    │
     │    distinct tamper error. This                                          │
     │    makes "Phase 10 cannot start before Phase 9 approval" a mechanical   │
     │    property of the loader Phase                                         │
     │    10+ code would naturally reach for, not a documentation convention   │
     │    someone could bypass by                                              │
     │    calling the wrong function.                                          │
     │ 3. External approval anchor: a new, separate record —                   │
     │    datasets_v3/PHASE9_APPROVAL.json — holding                           │
     │    {approved_registry_sha256, approved_commit, approved_date}, written  │
     │    by a distinct code path the                                          │
     │    normal freeze/regeneration script never calls. approved_commit is    │
     │    the SHA of the correction                                            │
     │    commit that introduces the exact registry content being approved —   │
     │    not a later status-                                                  │
     │    advancement commit — so the lineage reads candidate commit →         │
     │    approval record → (separately) the                                   │
     │    commit that advances LAST_COMPLETED_PHASE in CLAUDE.md. This         │
     │    correction builds the mechanism                                      │
     │    and both functions; it does not populate the anchor, because Phase 9 │
     │    isn't approved yet.                                                  │
     │    Populating it becomes the literal first, separate, auditable action  │
     │    once you approve — a few                                             │
     │    lines, one commit, distinct from all the code fixes here. A file     │
     │    inside the same writable repo is                                     │
     │    not an external security boundary by itself, so this is described    │
     │    precisely as a separately                                            │
     │    reviewed approval record anchored to the reviewed commit, not a      │
     │    cryptographic guarantee.                                             │
     │ 4. Bypass closure:                                                      │
     │    scan_strings/scan_operations/scan_compositions/held_out_values stop  │
     │    accepting a bare dict via reg=. They accept only a                   │
     │    VerifiedCandidateRegistry instance (the                              │
     │    thin wrapper function 1 returns). Fault tests get a distinct,        │
     │    separately-named test-only                                           │
     │    constructor (_unverified_registry_for_tests()) that production code  │
     │    never imports — stated                                               │
     │    plainly that Python can't hard-enforce this, only naming convention  │
     │    plus a fault test asserting no                                       │
     │    production import path reaches the raw loader.                       │
     │ 5. Deep immutability, not just a frozen wrapper:                        │
     │    @dataclass(frozen=True) only blocks reassigning                      │
     │    the top-level attribute, not mutating a nested dict/list inside it.  │
     │    Fix: the wrapper stores the                                          │
     │    canonical registry as serialized JSON text; every accessor           │
     │    (.section(name), etc.) returns                                       │
     │    json.loads() of that stored text — a fresh deep copy on every read,  │
     │    so a caller mutating a                                               │
     │    returned object can never corrupt the stored original. Regression    │
     │    test: call an accessor, mutate                                       │
     │    the returned object in place, call the accessor again, assert the    │
     │    second result is unaffected.                                         │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.2 Allowed operations per field — 4 layers, and the subtraction now    │
     │ provably works, because                                                 │
     │ there's only one vocabulary, not two. Rev 3/4's flaw: the semantic      │
     │ layer said employment → {filter, ranking} while the held-out-families   │
     │ constant is {argmax_topk, group_by, limit_only} —                       │
     │ "ranking" != "argmax_topk", so a literal set-subtraction semantic -     │
     │ held_out would never actually                                           │
     │ remove ranking, silently leaving it training-eligible (the opposite of  │
     │ intended, and worse than                                                │
     │ before). Fix: stop inventing softer synonyms for the semantic layer —   │
     │ reuse the exact frozen                                                  │
     │ construct names everywhere, so eligibility subtraction is a plain,      │
     │ provably-correct set difference                                         │
     │ on identical strings, not a translation the code could get wrong:       │
     │ 1. field_semantic_operations — what's meaningful for a field, including │
     │    held-out operations                                                  │
     │    where they make sense, named with the same literal strings as        │
     │    HELD_OUT_OPERATIONS                                                  │
     │    (holdout_v3.py's existing frozen constant) wherever applicable:      │
     │    employment →                                                         │
     │    {filter, argmax_topk} (not "ranking"); child-table fields            │
     │    (certifications/processes/                                           │
     │    services) and categorical company fields → {filter, aggregation,     │
     │    group_by}.                                                           │
     │    aggregation here means ungrouped scalar aggregation only (COUNT/SUM  │
     │    with no GROUP BY)                                                    │
     │    — a sibling of group_by, never a parent/hierarchy containing it,     │
     │    resolving the ambiguity                                              │
     │    directly: the three already-frozen held-out names (argmax_topk,      │
     │    group_by, limit_only) are                                            │
     │    never subtypes of anything else in this taxonomy, they're leaves.    │
     │ 2. query_level_constructs — argmax_topk, group_by, limit_only, tagged   │
     │    as structural/                                                       │
     │    query-shape operations that pair with an eligible field from layer 1 │
     │    (limit_only is                                                       │
     │    field-agnostic — arbitrary row sampling, doesn't require a field     │
     │    pairing at all, so it's excluded                                     │
     │    globally regardless of any per-field policy — see the fault test in  │
     │    E for this specific case).                                           │
     │ 3. field_specific_restrictions — sourced verbatim from README, not      │
     │    invented: Primary OEMs                                               │
     │    excluded from group_by/argmax_topk (composite-string reason,         │
     │    README:537-538); Address gets                                        │
     │    no aggregation of any kind (README:538); row_id — join always        │
     │    allowed, filter allowed                                              │
     │    only when the question explicitly names a record (README:541-543);   │
     │    company — filtering                                                  │
     │    unrestricted.                                                        │
     │ 4. field_training_eligible_operations (derived) =                       │
     │    field_semantic_operations[f] - HELD_OUT_OPERATIONS (literal set      │
     │    difference on the shared vocabulary, machine-tested by asserting     │
     │    this equation for every field), further constrained by layer 3's     │
     │    named restrictions. Evaluation/                                      │
     │    probe generation (Phase 22) consumes layers 1+3 directly, unfiltered │
     │    by the subtraction, since the                                        │
     │    operation-heldout probe specifically needs those constructs to exist │
     │    in dev/test.                                                         │
     │ 5. This per-field map is a candidate-generation-time heuristic, never   │
     │    the authoritative                                                    │
     │    eligibility gate. The real, existing gate — already frozen, fixed in │
     │    D.4 — is running the actual                                          │
     │    SQL-construct scanner (operation_families_present) against a task's  │
     │    actual rendered gold_sql                                             │
     │    at generation time; D.2's map only narrows which field+operation     │
     │    combinations are worth                                               │
     │    attempting to generate in the first place. Fault tests must exercise │
     │    real constructed SQL strings                                         │
     │    through the scanner (e.g. a bare SELECT company FROM companies LIMIT │
     │    5 — field-agnostic,                                                  │
     │    excluded regardless of which field's policy was consulted), not      │
     │    merely check whether a forbidden                                     │
     │    name string appears in a policy list.                                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Taxonomy names (filter, aggregation, join, semantic_filter, plus the 3  │
     │ frozen held-out                                                         │
     │ names): traced against every operation-shaped mention in README Phases  │
     │ 12, 14, 18-26, 41 —                                                     │
     │ aggregation and join are the document's own words for real mechanisms   │
     │ (README:264,539,541);                                                   │
     │ no_match/abstention was checked and confirmed to be an                  │
     │ evaluation-outcome axis (Phase 25),                                     │
     │ correctly excluded from this taxonomy. Independently cross-checked      │
     │ against v2's actual                                                     │
     │ taxonomy.py (FILTER_LIST, AGGREGATE covering                            │
     │ count/sum/group-by/argmax/top-k,                                        │
     │ SEMANTIC_FILTER for free-text columns) — the two sources converge on    │
     │ the same core names, and v2                                             │
     │ surfaces semantic_filter as the right category for                      │
     │ companies.product_or_service (a free-text                               │
     │ field with no v3 precedent otherwise). Still flagged for your explicit  │
     │ sign-off since neither                                                  │
     │ README nor v2 assembles this exact list as a single named per-field     │
     │ contract — Phase 9 is where it                                          │
     │ gets assembled for the first time, now grounded in two independent,     │
     │ converging sources rather than                                          │
     │ invented from nothing.                                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.3 Training eligibility. As above (layer 4), kept structurally         │
     │ separate from semantic validity                                         │
     │ (layer 1) so Phase 22's probe and future training generators consume    │
     │ the correct layer.                                                      │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.4 SQL operation detection — comment-safe lexer, not raw stripping. A  │
     │ left-to-right scanner                                                   │
     │ that replaces (never deletes) each '...' string literal, "..." / `...`  │
     │ / [...]                                                                 │
     │ quoted-identifier span, -- ... line comment, and /* ... */ block        │
     │ comment with a single space —                                           │
     │ preserving token boundaries so GROUP/**/BY becomes GROUP BY             │
     │ (space-separated), not GROUPBY                                          │
     │ (concatenated). Keyword-boundary regex (\bGROUP\s+BY\b, \bORDER\s+BY\b, │
     │ \bLIMIT\b,                                                              │
     │ case-insensitive) then runs on the cleaned remainder. Full test matrix: │
     │ GROUP/**/BY (detect),                                                   │
     │ GROUP\nBY (detect), GROUP  BY (detect), SELECT 'LIMIT' AS x (must NOT   │
     │ detect — inside string                                                  │
     │ literal), SELECT "GROUP BY" FROM t (must NOT detect — quoted            │
     │ identifier), SELECT `GROUP BY` FROM t                                   │
     │ (must NOT detect — backtick identifier), SELECT [GROUP BY] FROM t (must │
     │ NOT detect — bracket                                                    │
     │ identifier), SELECT group_id FROM t (must NOT detect — word boundary    │
     │ already excludes this),                                                 │
     │ escaped-quote cases ('it''s', "a""b") handled correctly by the          │
     │ scanner's escape-doubling rule.                                         │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.5 Exposure scanner. List-only: scan_strings(list[str]) -> report. A   │
     │ bare str raises                                                         │
     │ TypeError naming the expected type — single, non-contradictory contract │
     │ (Rev 1's self-contradiction                                             │
     │ is fully resolved, not just relabeled).                                 │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.6 Exposure-report assertions — three typed functions, not one generic │
     │ one. Each report shape                                                  │
     │ already has its own evidence counter in the current code                │
     │ (strings_scanned, sql_scanned,                                          │
     │ sets_scanned/composition_violations — confirmed to exist now, not       │
     │ hypothetical):                                                          │
     │ assert_value_scan_verified(report),                                     │
     │ assert_operation_scan_verified(report),                                 │
     │ assert_composition_scan_verified(report) — each hardcodes which fields  │
     │ must be present/consistent                                              │
     │ for its own shape. No caller ever names an arbitrary counter field,     │
     │ closing the                                                             │
     │ counter="wrong_field" bypass. Four states per type: pending             │
     │ (scanned:false,count:null — valid,                                      │
     │ never a pass), verified-zero (scanned:true, evidence counter >0,        │
     │ exposure_count:0,                                                       │
     │ internally consistent per-item/total), exposure-detected (fails),       │
     │ malformed (missing/inconsistent                                         │
     │ fields — fails).                                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.7 Exposure normalization — NFKC, not NFC (verified, not assumed). Ran │
     │ the actual case:                                                        │
     │ unicodedata.normalize('NFC', 'ＡＳ９１００') returns the fullwidth      │
     │ string unchanged (does not                                              │
     │ equal 'AS9100'); NFKC on the same input correctly folds it to 'AS9100'. │
     │ NFC only normalizes                                                     │
     │ canonical equivalence (e.g. accented composition); it does not fold     │
     │ compatibility variants                                                  │
     │ (fullwidth forms, and similar). Corrected pipeline:                     │
     │ Unicode-compatibility-normalize (NFKC) →                                │
     │ casefold → collapse internal whitespace runs → substring match, applied │
     │ to every held-out literal                                               │
     │ against every model-visible rendered string (not only raw KB cells —    │
     │ rendering/copying can alter                                             │
     │ representation even from ASCII sources), confined to the scanning step  │
     │ only (never mutates the                                                 │
     │ actual training text). "AS9100", "as9100", " AS9100 ", "ＡＳ９１００"   │
     │ all match; unrelated                                                    │
     │ substrings do not. Flagged for approval since this is a real scientific │
     │ definition of                                                           │
     │ "exposure," not a mechanically-derived default — biased toward          │
     │ over-detection deliberately (a false                                    │
     │ positive costs one extra row to inspect; a false negative is an actual  │
     │ leak).                                                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.8 Logical fingerprint (lfp2). Canonicalized logical_components folded │
     │ into the hash.                                                          │
     │ Commutative operands (two ANDed or two ORed predicates) sort before     │
     │ hashing so reordering doesn't                                           │
     │ change the fingerprint; the operator itself and any differing           │
     │ predicate/value do change it. Nested                                    │
     │ trees (A AND (B OR C) vs (A AND B) OR C) hash by canonical tree form,   │
     │ not flattened. Missing/                                                 │
     │ incomplete logical_components fails closed rather than silently falling │
     │ back to a weaker hash.                                                  │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.9 Multipart representation — redesigned in this revision. The         │
     │ UNION-ALL-with-discriminator                                            │
     │ design from Rev 3/4 is withdrawn; it doesn't work. Constructive proof:  │
     │ UNION ALL requires equal                                                │
     │ column arity across every branch, so a scalar part (val) and a          │
     │ two-column part (company, county)                                       │
     │ cannot share one result shape without padding; the shared part_id, val  │
     │ schema also throws away                                                 │
     │ each part's real column names, forces every value through CAST(... AS   │
     │ TEXT) (turning 3 into                                                   │
     │ "3", which the existing scalar grader's _SCALAR_OK type check would     │
     │ then treat as a different                                               │
     │ value than an untouched gold 3), and — worse — would require the        │
     │ model's own predicted SQL to                                            │
     │ independently reproduce that exact discriminator/CAST convention just   │
     │ to be gradable, teaching an                                             │
     │ artificial SQL-shape requirement that has nothing to do with the actual │
     │ question. Withdrawn.                                                    │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Replacement design: an ordered/keyed collection of                      │
     │ independently-executed, independently-typed                             │
     │ per-part results — no shared schema, no discriminator, no casting.      │
     │ - gold_sql for a multi_part task is a dict keyed by part_id, one        │
     │   independently normal SQL                                              │
     │   string per declared part (e.g. {"count": "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM   │
     │   ...", "companies": "SELECT company FROM ..."}), each executed on its  │
     │   own, producing its own natural SQLResult                              │
     │   with its own real column names and native types. This still honors    │
     │   Phase 12's "D's target is a                                           │
     │   query" framing as its natural generalization for the multi-part case: │
     │   a keyed sequence of                                                   │
     │   queries, not one query straining to represent several shapes at once. │
     │ - The model's predicted SQL for a multi-part task is a sequence of      │
     │   statements (split on                                                  │
     │   top-level ; using the same comment/quote-aware lexer built for D.4,   │
     │   so a semicolon inside a                                               │
     │   string literal is never mistaken for a statement boundary), executed  │
     │   in the order the question                                             │
     │   presents the parts (order is part of the frozen task, known to both   │
     │   the model via the prompt and                                          │
     │   the grader via parts[] — nothing is invented at grading time). Each   │
     │   statement is paired                                                   │
     │   positionally with the corresponding declared part.                    │
     │ - Grading: a new thin wrapper, grade_multipart(item, pred_results:      │
     │   dict, gold_results: dict) -> GradeResult, calls the existing,         │
     │   unmodified compare_results once per declared part (its own            │
     │   answer_type/target_columns), and requires every declared part correct │
     │   — no new comparison                                                   │
     │   algorithm, full reuse of frozen Phase 7 semantics per part.           │
     │ - Empty vs. omitted parts are now cleanly distinguishable, closing the  │
     │   Rev 4 ambiguity: an emitted                                           │
     │   statement that executes and returns 0 rows is a legitimate empty-set  │
     │   answer for that part, graded                                          │
     │   normally; an omitted statement (fewer statements than declared parts) │
     │   is a missing-required-part                                            │
     │   failure. No shared-table ambiguity to resolve.                        │
     │ - Top-k ordering, real column names, and native types are preserved     │
     │   automatically — each part's                                           │
     │   SQLResult is exactly what that part's own SELECT naturally returns,   │
     │   nothing is regrouped or                                               │
     │   reinterpreted after the fact.                                         │
     │ - EvalRecord.execution_result for a multi-part item becomes a dict      │
     │   keyed by part_id, each value                                          │
     │   the natural (columns, rows) pair for that part — still one            │
     │   JSON-serializable field, still                                        │
     │   trivially round-trips through save/reload/regrade; the parts metadata │
     │   field says which                                                      │
     │   answer_type/target_columns apply to which key.                        │
     │ - Modality-independent contract, addressing the layering concern        │
     │   directly: Phase 9 freezes the                                         │
     │   property that a multi-part answer is a part_id-keyed collection of    │
     │   independently-typed                                                   │
     │   part-results, each graded via the existing single-part                │
     │   compare_results semantics using that                                  │
     │   part's own answer_type/target_columns. D produces this via a keyed    │
     │   sequence of independent                                               │
     │   SQL executions (above). How C's raw model completion gets parsed into │
     │   this same keyed-result                                                │
     │   shape remains a Phase 11/13 concern, correctly out of Phase 9's scope │
     │   — but Phase 9 now freezes                                             │
     │   the target representation both modalities must produce, not just D's  │
     │   mechanism, so grading,                                                │
     │   EvalRecord, and regrading are written once and work for either        │
     │   modality without later                                                │
     │   reconciliation. (Confirmed: no v2 precedent exists for this either    │
     │   way — see Context.)                                                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.10 Extra-part rule — settled now, not deferred. Extends the existing, │
     │ already-frozen                                                          │
     │ precedent (phase7_grader_tests.py's                                     │
     │ metrics_differ_semantic_right_schema_wrong: an extra column             │
     │ scores task_result_correctness=1.0 but                                  │
     │ strict_result_schema_accuracy=0.0): an extra,                           │
     │ undeclared part present in the executed/tagged result beyond what       │
     │ parts[] declares does not                                               │
     │ fail task_result_correctness (each declared part is still graded        │
     │ independently and correctly) but                                        │
     │ does fail strict_result_schema_accuracy (output includes something      │
     │ outside the declared schema).                                           │
     │ Missing required parts[] metadata on a multi_part-typed item fails      │
     │ closed with a clear error —                                             │
     │ never silently falls back to legacy per-column grading. Legacy fallback │
     │ (flattened                                                              │
     │ target_columns-as-parts) applies only to items explicitly predating     │
     │ parts_list_v1 (a fixed,                                                 │
     │ named allowlist of legacy fixture IDs, not "any item missing parts"),   │
     │ so a future generator bug                                               │
     │ that omits parts[] cannot silently masquerade as a legacy item.         │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.11 Grading. As D.9/D.10. GRADER_VERSION bumped grade_v3.0 →           │
     │ grade_v3.1.                                                             │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.12 EvalRecord/result schema. Optional parts: tuple | None = None,     │
     │ backward-compatible                                                     │
     │ from_dict default. build_fixtures() extended with a                     │
     │ populated-execution_result multipart                                    │
     │ fixture pair specifically to prove regrade() recomputation: one         │
     │ deliberately-wrong multipart                                            │
     │ answer that the current (buggy) grader would have scored correct,       │
     │ regraded under the fixed                                                │
     │ grader to confirm it now scores incorrect — proving the regrade path    │
     │ genuinely recomputes rather                                             │
     │ than re-stamping provenance on a stale score.                           │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.13 Verification/regrading. regrade() re-invokes                       │
     │ compare_results/grade_structured                                        │
     │ against retained execution_result/gold (per-part where applicable)      │
     │ instead of keeping the                                                  │
     │ recorded outcome for well-formed predictions. Raw prediction and gold   │
     │ remain untouched (existing                                              │
     │ _replace() invariant preserved).                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.17 Multi-part execution-failure semantics — new in this revision,     │
     │ closing Gap #7/#8 from the                                              │
     │ Rev 5 coverage check. Amended once more after direct verification of    │
     │ three follow-up corrections.                                            │
     │ Grounded in grade_v3.py's existing single-query contract (re-read in    │
     │ full): grade_structured                                                 │
     │ re-raises X.ScopeError rather than swallowing it, checks whole-response │
     │ degeneracy                                                              │
     │ (classify_prediction_text, including stopped_at_max_new_tokens) before  │
     │ any parsing or                                                          │
     │ execution happens at all, and otherwise reduces every failure to the    │
     │ existing closed status                                                  │
     │ vocabulary via that same function. Multi-part grading reuses this exact │
     │ machinery, adding only an                                               │
     │ aggregation rule across parts:                                          │
     │ - Whole-response truncation/degeneracy is checked once, before any      │
     │   statement-splitting or                                                │
     │   execution — mirroring the single-query contract exactly               │
     │   (grade_v3.py's comment: "Partial or                                   │
     │   degenerate output is NEVER parsed or executed"). If                   │
     │   classify_prediction_text returns a status for                         │
     │   the raw multi-part response                                           │
     │   (truncated_output/generation_failure/invalid_output), the whole       │
     │   item takes that status immediately; the statement-splitter and every  │
     │   part's executor are never                                             │
     │   invoked. Regression test: a response flagged                          │
     │   stopped_at_max_new_tokens must result in zero                         │
     │   executor calls across all declared parts — verified by call-count,    │
     │   not just by final status.                                             │
     │ - Each declared part that survives the whole-response check is graded   │
     │   through the same,                                                     │
     │   unmodified per-part pipeline (execute → compare_results) — no new     │
     │   failure-classification logic                                          │
     │   beyond the two additions below.                                       │
     │ - X.ScopeError is re-raised immediately if any part's execution raises  │
     │   it — never swallowed                                                  │
     │   into a per-part failure status, preserving the existing invariant     │
     │   that a scope violation is a                                           │
     │   harness bug, not an ordinary incorrect answer.                        │
     │ - An omitted required statement (D.9: fewer statements than declared    │
     │   parts) is classified as                                               │
     │   parse_failure for that part — consistent with the existing use of     │
     │   parse_failure for                                                     │
     │   "prediction doesn't have the expected structure" (grade_structured's  │
     │   own "not a SELECT/WITH                                                │
     │   query" case), not a new category.                                     │
     │ - The full per-part failure set now explicitly includes timeout         │
     │   alongside SQL_error,                                                  │
     │   parse_failure, generation_failure, invalid_output (the whole-response │
     │   check already covers                                                  │
     │   truncated_output) — timeout was missing from the Rev 6 list despite   │
     │   being one of CLAUDE.md's                                              │
     │   frozen eight statuses.                                                │
     │ - If every part executes and compares cleanly: overall status =         │
     │   "correct" iff every part is                                           │
     │   correct (already frozen in D.9/D.10), else "incorrect".               │
     │ - If one or more (post-whole-response-check) parts hit a per-part       │
     │   failure status: the whole item's                                      │
     │   task_result_correctness and strict_result_schema_accuracy are 0.0,    │
     │   and the top-level status                                              │
     │   is set from the first such failure by declared part order (a small,   │
     │   explicit, new tie-break —                                             │
     │   flagged for approval, analogous in spirit to the existing             │
     │   OPERATION_PRECEDENCE pattern already                                  │
     │   used elsewhere in holdout_v3.py) — never silently reclassified as     │
     │   plain "incorrect", since that                                         │
     │   would hide why it failed. Per-part failure details (which part, which │
     │   status) are retained in                                               │
     │   error_detail, not discarded.                                          │
     │ - Fault/regression tests: whole-response truncation → zero executor     │
     │   calls (new); a correct first                                          │
     │   part followed by a SQL_error second part (must not score correct,     │
     │   must retain the real failure                                          │
     │   type); a timeout in a part (now covered, wasn't before); an omitted   │
     │   statement → parse_failure,                                            │
     │   not left unclassified; a ScopeError in any part (must propagate, not  │
     │   be caught); a parse_failure                                           │
     │   in a non-first part (tests the aggregation rule isn't just "check     │
     │   part 0"); all-parts-correct                                           │
     │   baseline (must still score correct, no regression).                   │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.18 Operation-heldout and compositional-heldout scanning must cover    │
     │ every part, not the dict's                                              │
     │ keys — new in this revision, and this is a live, reproduced bug in the  │
     │ D.9 design, not a                                                       │
     │ documentation gap. Reproduced directly: calling the existing            │
     │ scan_operations with a                                                  │
     │ part_id-keyed gold_sql dict (as D.9 defines it) iterates the dict's     │
     │ keys                                                                    │
     │ ("count", "companies") as if they were SQL text — enumerate(strings)    │
     │ over a dict yields its                                                  │
     │ keys. Verified with a synthetic two-part query where one part contains  │
     │ a bare LIMIT: passing the                                               │
     │ dict directly reports 0 exposures; passing list(gold_sql.values())      │
     │ correctly reports 1. This                                               │
     │ would have silently let a held-out construct into training the moment   │
     │ D.9 shipped. Fix:                                                       │
     │ - scan_operations/scan_compositions (and scan_strings, for symmetry     │
     │   with D.5) raise on a                                                  │
     │   bare dict rather than silently iterating it — consistent with the     │
     │   list-only philosophy already                                          │
     │   adopted in D.5, fail loud instead of fail silent.                     │
     │ - New dedicated wrapper, scan_operations_multipart(gold_sql: dict,      │
     │   reg), explicitly extracts                                             │
     │   gold_sql.values() before delegating to the existing (unmodified)      │
     │   scan_operations, then combines                                        │
     │   detected families across all parts using the existing frozen          │
     │   precedence                                                            │
     │   (OPERATION_PRECEDENCE) — a multi-part task with group_by in one part  │
     │   and a clean filter in                                                 │
     │   another is excluded from training entirely, exactly as a single-query │
     │   task would be under the                                               │
     │   existing multi_family_rule. Per README:722, this check applies to D's │
     │   SQL and C's metadata                                                  │
     │   alike — C's metadata (once Phase 11/13 generates it) must be derived  │
     │   from the same complete,                                               │
     │   all-parts task evidence, not just part 1.                             │
     │ - Constructs are never concatenated across parts before classification  │
     │   (an ORDER BY in one part                                              │
     │   and a LIMIT in a different part must not be misread as one            │
     │   argmax_topk query) — each part is                                     │
     │   classified independently, and the union of families found across      │
     │   parts is what's checked                                               │
     │   against the held-out set, not a merged/concatenated SQL string.       │
     │ - Fault tests: the exact reproduced case above (dict-direct call → must │
     │   now raise, not silently                                               │
     │   return 0); a two-part task with a held-out construct in the non-first │
     │   part → whole task excluded;                                           │
     │   a two-part task with clean SQL in both parts → not excluded; an ORDER │
     │   BY in part A and LIMIT                                                │
     │   in part B (different parts) → must NOT be misclassified as a single   │
     │   argmax_topk construct.                                                │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.19 Compositional-heldout checking must use the whole task's component │
     │ union — new in this                                                     │
     │ revision. Grounded directly in README's Phase 23 superset rule          │
     │ (re-read: "For each held-out set H                                      │
     │ and every training set T: assert not H ⊆ T") — a multi-part task is one │
     │ logical training item, so                                               │
     │ its "training set T" for this purpose must be the union of every        │
     │ declared part's component usage,                                        │
     │ not each part checked in isolation. Confirmed by construction: a part   │
     │ carrying only                                                           │
     │ {certifications} and a second part of the same task carrying only       │
     │ {processes} would each pass                                             │
     │ the held-out {certifications, processes} check individually while their │
     │ union violates it — exactly                                             │
     │ the leak the superset rule exists to prevent. Fix: scan_compositions    │
     │ for a multi-part task is                                                │
     │ called once with the union of component sets declared across all of     │
     │ that task's parts, not once                                             │
     │ per part. Per-part structure and join-arity information are retained    │
     │ separately (for provenance and                                          │
     │ for D.9's independent-execution design) — the union is computed only    │
     │ for the composition check                                               │
     │ itself, and never used to invent a join that never actually occurred in │
     │ any single part's SQL.                                                  │
     │ Fault test: reproduced the exact case above — checking parts separately │
     │ reports 0 violations;                                                   │
     │ checking the task-level union reports 1 — confirming the union-based    │
     │ check is required, not optional.                                        │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.20 Gold/prediction identification contract for multipart D — made     │
     │ explicit, not merely                                                    │
     │ implied. D.9 already specifies gold as a part_id-keyed dict and the     │
     │ model's prediction as a                                                 │
     │ positionally-ordered sequence of statements; this sub-contract freezes  │
     │ that pairing explicitly as                                              │
     │ its own named rule rather than leaving it as an incidental detail:      │
     │ parts[] order is                                                        │
     │ authoritative, and predicted statement N (1-indexed, in emission order) │
     │ belongs to declared part N.                                             │
     │ Test matrix, each case distinct from D.9's existing missing/extra-part  │
     │ tests: statements emitted out                                           │
     │ of the declared order (must be graded against the wrong part and        │
     │ therefore likely fail — this is a                                       │
     │ model-prediction quality issue, not a grading-contract bug, so the test │
     │ confirms positional pairing                                             │
     │ is applied literally, not smartly reordered); too few statements        │
     │ (missing-part case, D.9); too many                                      │
     │ statements (extra-part case, D.10); a semicolon inside a quoted string  │
     │ literal (must not be                                                    │
     │ misread as a statement boundary — reuses the D.4 lexer); an             │
     │ emitted-but-empty statement (a bare ;                                   │
     │ with nothing between two separators — treated as a parse_failure for    │
     │ that part, not a silently                                               │
     │ skipped one); duplicate or ambiguous part_ids in the task's own         │
     │ declared parts[] metadata (a                                            │
     │ task-authoring error — fails closed at task-validation time, before     │
     │ grading is even attempted).                                             │
     │                                                                         │
     │ D.21 Insufficient-evidence regrading — new in this revision. The field  │
     │ design is agreed (Codex has                                             │
     │ since clarified a ninth status was never a hard requirement, a separate │
     │ field is acceptable); what                                              │
     │ was still missing, and is verified as a real gap, is that the field     │
     │ alone doesn't stop anything from                                        │
     │ consuming a historical score as if freshly verified. Confirmed the      │
     │ underlying constraint by                                                │
     │ re-reading regrade()'s own docstring: it deliberately does not          │
     │ re-execute SQL ("Phase 8 uses                                           │
     │ synthetic execution results rather than live inference"), so a record   │
     │ whose execution_result is                                               │
     │ None genuinely cannot have its score re-derived — there's nothing to    │
     │ recompute from. The core rule:                                          │
     │ never relabel a historical score as newly recomputed when the evidence  │
     │ needed to recompute it is                                               │
     │ absent. Design: keep status within CLAUDE.md §25's frozen eight values, │
     │ untouched, when                                                         │
     │ evidence is insufficient — the original score stands as the historical  │
     │ record it always was. Add a                                             │
     │ separate, non-authoritative field, regrade_outcome: "recomputed" |      │
     │ "insufficient_evidence" | "not_attempted", alongside                    │
     │ status/grader_version/grader_sha256.                                    │
     │                                                                         │
     │ Verified consumer gap, not hypothetical: I read eval_report_v3.py's     │
     │ summarize() directly — it                                               │
     │ computes scored/failed/task/schema purely from                          │
     │ status/task_result_correctness/                                         │
     │ strict_result_schema_accuracy, with zero awareness of any               │
     │ regrade_outcome field. A record with a                                  │
     │ stale status="correct" and regrade_outcome="insufficient_evidence"      │
     │ would pass summarize()'s                                                │
     │ existing DenominatorError checks and be silently counted as an ordinary │
     │ verified-correct item —                                                 │
     │ exactly the "presented as freshly verified" failure mode. The field     │
     │ must be consumed, not just                                              │
     │ stored. Required additions:                                             │
     │ - eval_report_v3.summarize() gains an explicit regrade-coverage         │
     │   breakdown                                                             │
     │   ({"recomputed": N, "insufficient_evidence": M, "not_attempted": K})   │
     │   computed alongside the                                                │
     │   existing denominator accounting — without changing that accounting:   │
     │   an insufficient-evidence                                              │
     │   record still counts in scored/failed exactly per its retained status, │
     │   is never dropped from                                                 │
     │   the denominator, and is never treated as an automatic wrong answer.   │
     │ - A new function, eval_verify_v3.assert_fully_regraded(records), raises │
     │   if any record shows                                                   │
     │   regrade_outcome == "insufficient_evidence". Any report-generation     │
     │   path that wants to label its                                          │
     │   output "freshly regraded"/"fully re-verified under the current        │
     │   grader" must call this first and                                      │
     │   fail loudly rather than certify a claim it can't back. A report that  │
     │   hasn't cleared this gate must                                         │
     │   instead present those records' scores explicitly labeled as           │
     │   historical/unverified, not folded                                     │
     │   silently into headline numbers.                                       │
     │ - finetune/eval_report_v3.py added to the file inventory (C) — not      │
     │   previously listed.                                                    │
     │ - End-to-end test added: serialize → reload → regrade → verify →        │
     │   report, on a mixed batch                                              │
     │   including one insufficient-evidence record — confirms the record's    │
     │   original score/status survive                                         │
     │   unchanged, the coverage breakdown reports it distinctly, and          │
     │   assert_fully_regraded correctly                                       │
     │   raises for that batch. Records needing no regrade at all              │
     │   (pre-execution failures like                                          │
     │   generation_failure/truncated_output, derivable from retained          │
     │   raw_output/stop-metadata alone)                                       │
     │   get regrade_outcome: "recomputed" since their classification never    │
     │   depended on                                                           │
     │   execution_result. Flagged for your explicit sign-off, since the       │
     │   coverage-gate design (what                                            │
     │   exactly blocks a report from claiming "fully regraded") is a judgment │
     │   call worth your confirmation,                                         │
     │   not a purely mechanical fix.                                          │
     │                                                                         │

     v2 findings that changed this revision:
     - Operation taxonomy (D.2) — confirmed, with a refinement. v2's actual
       taxonomy.py uses
       exactly FILTER_LIST = "filter_list", AGGREGATE = "aggregate" (explicitly
       documented as
       covering "count / sum / group-by / argmax / top-k" under one umbrella),
       and
       SEMANTIC_FILTER = "semantic_filter" (free-text predicate matching over a
       product_service-style column). This independently converges with README's
       own vocabulary

       which is strong
       grounding rather than a second guess. It also surfaces something I'd
       missed: v3's schema has an
       analogous free-text column (companies.product_or_service), which behaves
       differently from an
       ordinary categorical filter (exact/enum match). Added semantic_filter to
       D.2 as a distinct,
       precedented category for that field, rather than forcing it into plain
       filter.
     - Multipart representation (D.9) — checked, no precedent exists. v2's
       grade.py has no
       structured heterogeneous multi-part concept at all; its only parts = 
       re.split(...) usage
       (line 163) is a free-text recall grader splitting a semicolon-joined
       string gold answer for a
       "contains all substrings" text match — unrelated to a scalar+set
       SQL-result multi-part answer.
       Stated plainly: there is no v2 shortcut for D.9. It is a v3-native design
       problem, addressed
       fresh below, not ported.
     - Regrade design (D.13) — confirmed, not contradicted. v2's regrade.py
       docstring states
       explicitly: "Nothing here re-runs the model... No model was re-run: this
       re-scores" retained
       evidence using current grading logic. That is exactly the shape of the v3
       fix proposed below
       (re-apply current grading logic to retained evidence, don't re-run
       inference) — v2 precedent
       validates the design rather than suggesting a different one.
